newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-INDIANS PITCHER JOSE MESA ACQUITTED OF RAPE CHARGES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-INDIANS PITCHER JOSE MESA ACQUITTED OF RAPE CHARGES.

text.p: Cleveland Indians star relief pitcher Jose Mesa was acquitted of rape and three lesser counts of gross sexual imposition by an Ohio court on Wednesday.
A Cuyohoga County jury of seven women and five men also found Mesa not guilty on a charge of theft. Mesa faces a separate trial on a gun charge.

The 30-year-old Mesa appeared to show little emotion when the verdict of the most serious charge of rape was announced first. After he was found not guilty of all charges a relieved Mesa broke down in tears and was comforted by his legal team.
Jury deliberations had resumed Wednesday morning after they failed to reach a verdict following more than four hours of deliberations on Tuesday.

Mesa faced three to 10 years in prison if convicted of rape. Judge Thomas Curran ruled Monday that the panel could consider the lesser charge of gross sexual imposition -- a felony that carries a penalty of six to 18 months in jail -- after throwing out a felony assault charge.
The defence elected not to call any witnesses to the stand in the trial, which began last Monday.
Mesa and a friend were indicted on charges stemming from a December 22 incident in Lakewood, Ohio.
Mesa's friend, David Blanco, 34, pleaded innocent to one count of gross sexual imposition and one count of carrying a concealed weapon. His trial will be held separately.
According to the Lakewood Police Department's report, two 26-year-old females complained that the two men sexually molested them in a Lakewood motel.
The report states that Mesa and Blanco met the women in the popular downtown Cleveland area called The Flats, and Mesa took one woman's purse to entice her into his vehicle.
The women told police that they went into the motel with the intention of using the restroom, retrieving the purse and leaving. Mesa and Blanco allegedly began fondling the women.
The woman who testified last week that Mesa had raped her admitted she was drunk at the time and did not take several opportunities to escape.
"This was especially bad for my kids," said Mesa's wife Mirla, who called the trial difficult.
"We felt especially sorry for them because they really didn't know what was going on."
Jose and Mirla Mesa have five children ages three to 13.
The Indians had been granted a roster exemption for Mesa while he was standing trial.

Mesa appeared in 69 games for the Indians last season, recording 39 saves and posting a 2-7 record with a 3.73 ERA. The Dominican native finished second in voting for the 1995 American League Cy Young Award when he posted a club-record 46 saves in helping the Indians reach the World Series.
